label: Sixth-edition aphorisms
title: Aphorism § 23
text:
§ 23



 All pure experience, however, and all accurate research convince us
          that persistent symptoms of disease are far from being removed and annihilated by opposite
          symptoms of medicines (as in the antipathic, enantiopathic or palliative method), that, on
          the contrary, after transient, apparent alleviation, they break forth again, only with
          increased intensity, and become manifestly aggravated (see § 58 - 62 and 69).
